_source: docs/spec/APPLICATION_GAP_SPEC.md §2 tables ①, ②, ②-bis. THE SPEC IS THE AUTHORITY; this file is its machine-readable form. Adding a gap means adding a row HERE and in the spec - never inventing one in code. `ledger/gaps.py` refuses to run when this file and the declaration disagree, in either direction.
_register_shares_one_name_across_three_s: APPLICATION_GAP_SPEC 2026-08-31: the operator does the SAME thing for all three - fetch the registration record - so it is one name with the type swapped in. A fourth subject needs no new name.
_why_names_live_outside_the_code: A label in code is a second authority that goes stale without anybody noticing. The detector emits declaration names and looks the label up here, so a spec revision is a data change.

object_sides._kept_on_purpose: APPLICATION_GAP_SPEC: dropping the row sends the next person to ask the same question again. `gaps.vacuous_types` marks it not-applicable MECHANICALLY - processed_with is recipe@1's only appearance in the vocabulary, so a recipe without one cannot exist - and the row is what carries that reason to the screen.
